description: Vulnerable Dockerfile with simulated security attack logs

expected_findings.title: Container Running as Root
expected_evidence: No non-root USER instruction is present
expected_remediation: Run the application using the non-root user

expected_findings.title: Hardcoded Credential
expected_evidence: AWS_SECRET_KEY is assigned a hardcoded value
expected_remediation: Recommend rotation if the credential is real

additional_checks.title: Base Image Security
additional_checks.expected_observation: The base image uses Python 3.9 and is not pinned to an immutable digest

expected_conclusions: All three events originate from the same IP address
Events occurred within a short time window
The logs do not confirm successful compromise

patch_requirements: Create and use a non-root application user
forbidden_conclusions: Claiming that the attacker successfully compromised the container
Claiming that EXPOSE 22 alone makes SSH publicly accessible
Claiming that one failed login event proves repeated brute-force attempts
Claiming the patch was tested when no external tests were performed
Claiming the example credential is a confirmed valid secret
